open_decisions.question: In AUDPROC the audit timestamp is moved into AUD-TIMESTAMP (line 74) and then overwritten by the group move of the 32-byte system information into the 58-byte AUD-HEADER (line 75), so the written audit record carries neither the timestamp nor correctly aligned system/user/program/terminal values. On open failure the program also closes the unopened audit file. Must the forward audit service reproduce the record exactly as written today, or write the timestamp and the system, user, program and terminal identifiers in their own fields?

Copybook AUDITLOG declares audit types ('TRAN','USER','SYST'; BR-143), actions (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, INQUIRE, LOGIN, LOGOUT, STARTUP, SHUTDOWN; BR-144) and outcome statuses ('SUCC','FAIL','WARN'; BR-145). Callers assign them and AUDPROC writes them unchecked. Must the forward audit service reject values outside these domains, or record whatever the caller supplies (as implemented)?

DB2ERR (line 75) uses the non-standard 'ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP'; the ERRPROC logic file flags the same construct (line 57) and PORTDEL uses it for the deletion audit timestamp (source line 169). Which compiler extension is in use and what timestamp format do ERRLOG rows, error-log records and deletion audit records actually carry?

Fifteen elementary level-01 items (e.g. HISTLD00 WS-COMMIT-THRESHOLD, the REPORT-RECORD print lines, DB2CONN WS-CONNECTION-STATE/WS-RETRY-COUNT/WS-MAX-RETRIES, DB2CMT WS-SAVEPOINT-ID) are catalogued as record-level items without Field IDs, so no Java type could be assigned. Should the reverse harness register Field IDs for them, or may later stages map them at record level using the catalogued PIC?

AUDPROC appends audit records to a sequential dataset (DD AUDFILE, OPEN EXTEND per call), its group MOVE LS-SYSTEM-INFO TO AUD-HEADER may overwrite the timestamp just set, and it CLOSEs the file after a failed OPEN; RPTAUD00 meanwhile reads an indexed audit file keyed AUD-KEY (DD AUDITLOG) built on the same copybook. Is there one audit trail (and which organisation), and must the timestamp overwrite be reproduced?

PORTMSTR FD PORTFOLIO-FILE says RECORD CONTAINS 100 CHARACTERS (line 32) but PORTFOLIO-RECORD fields total 103 bytes, and the caller exchanges a 100-byte LS-PORTFOLIO. Which physical record length is authoritative for PORTFILE (100 or 103), and should the trailing FILLER be shortened?

PORTMSTR 2100-LOG-PORTFOLIO-UPDATE (live after every successful update) builds LS-AUDIT-REQUEST and CALLs AUDPROC, and the dead 2100-HANDLE-VSAM-ERROR builds LS-ERROR-REQUEST for ERRPROC, but 35 data names (LS-AUDIT-REQUEST, LS-*, PORT-KEY, PORT-RECORD, WS-BEFORE-IMAGE, USERID, TERMINAL-ID, ERR-*) are declared nowhere. Which copybooks were intended (for example the AUDPROC request copybook and ERRHAND), or should the audit call be redesigned?

ERRPROC's LINKAGE LS-ERROR-REQUEST is 354 bytes, but DB2ERR (line 199) and DB2STAT (line 227) CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE from copybook ERRHAND (about 370 bytes, different field order). Which layout is the contract of the Java error service?

Error paths do not stop as expected: PORTADD and PORTDEL continue the read loop on closed files after an open failure (returning RC 8), and PORTMSTR's 9000-ERROR GOBACKs from inside a PERFORM after closing a possibly unopened file. Should Java reproduce this behaviour or end the step/call immediately with RC 8?

PORTADD and PORTDEL (key PORT-KEY, PORTFLIO layout) and PORTMSTR (key PORT-ID, 103-byte PORTFOLIO-RECORD) all ASSIGN TO PORTFILE as an indexed file. Do they address the same VSAM dataset, and if so which record layout and key are authoritative?

Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.

Which portfolio status domain is authoritative? PORTMSTR validates 'A', 'I', 'C' (VALID-STATUS, BR-095) while copybook PORTFLIO used by PORTADD and PORTDEL declares 'A' active, 'C' closed, 'S' suspended (BR-149); 'I' and 'S' each exist in only one place, and the PORTFLIO and PORTMSTR records are linked only by naming convention (REL-002, GAP-091). What do 'I' and 'S' mean, and do PORTMSTR and the batch programs maintain the same portfolio master?

2100-LOG-PORTFOLIO-UPDATE (18 names) and the unreachable 2100-HANDLE-VSAM-ERROR (17 names) use 35 data names that are not declared in PORTMSTR, which has no COPY statements, so the program would not compile as written. Which copybooks (ERRHAND, AUDITLOG?) are meant to be included, what audit request content does AUDPROC receive for a successful update, and is 2100-HANDLE-VSAM-ERROR retired?

9000-ERROR ends the call with GOBACK inside a PERFORM (line 237); WS-ERROR-TEXT is set on every error path ('Invalid command', 'Invalid Portfolio ID format', 'Portfolio Name is required', 'Portfolio not found', ...) but is never passed to the caller or logged, so callers receive return code 8 without a message. Should the modern interface return the error text to the caller (or log it)?

FD PORTFOLIO-FILE in PORTMSTR declares RECORD CONTAINS 100 CHARACTERS (line 31), but the PORTFOLIO-RECORD fields total 103 bytes. What is the physical VSAM record length of the portfolio master used by PORTMSTR?
